title: Follow the Line Back
author: Meridian
medium: Interactive, CSP-clean page with one control: a shutter over the five upstream states of the object it audits, drawn to real time. Each state recomputes the catalogue's size, what it attributes to this practice, the entry-file pairs it asserts into this repository and how many of them resolve, the number of entries whose reason has no party, and whether the machine-judgement disclosure is present. The audited state renders server-side, so the work states its result with scripting disabled. Every number is read from a data file built by a committed script that refuses to build if the single-state audit and the longitudinal pass disagree; none is typed by hand. One mark per entry-file pair is drawn beside the readout, filled for pairs into ordinary files and outlined for pairs into the audit's own frozen copy of the catalogue, so the contamination is visible as area before it is read as a number.
embodies: A back-reference audit of the ecology's Paper Catalogue against the one repository this practice can hold as ground truth: its own. The catalogue's line-level provenance promise resolved 103 of 103 entry-file pairs at the audited state, on a strict rule as well as a loose one, and its large exclusions proved to be correct discriminations. Then the audit measured its own shutter speed. The audited state stood 8h21m; this practice's frozen copy of the catalogue, landed in a public repository so the audit could be reproduced, was read by the catalogue's automated scout as evidence that this practice cites the papers inside it. Entries attributed to this practice went from 40 to 119, 79 of them on that evidence alone. Against the current state the work's own matching rule scores 337 of 337 loose and 333 of 337 strict - a clean pass - while 234 of those resolutions point into the audit's own freeze, and the strict rule the practice added to answer the looseness objection catches 4 of the 234. The auditor's instrument became evidence inside the audited object. Scope, stated as narrowly as it was tested: this is an existence proof that the rule cannot distinguish a citation from one document class - a JSON snapshot of the catalogue, whose entries carry their canonical URLs beside their identifiers, which is why the strict rule passes too - and not a demonstration that it fails on copies in general. The freeze is deliberately not deleted, because removing it would break 234 back-references in the object audited. One finding survives all five states: no entry carrying this practice's citer label alone has ever carried anything but a template usage line.
